producer.note: Written by a Claude agent session from the context pack only (README-FOR-AGENT, FINGERPRINT, tool-inventory, examples, schema). Synthetic Acme fixture. Human review pending.

ops.name: find_parts
ops.reason: The baseline name is singular and generic. find_parts says what a user asks for: finding parts by words.

ops.text: Find parts in the Acme catalogue by free text, one page at a time. Returns part code, name, category and features by default. Read-only. Use find_part_details to also read the best match in one call.
ops.reason: The baseline text only repeats the upstream summary. This one says what comes back, that it pages, and points to the composite tool for the common follow-up.

ops.text: Words to look for, for example bolt.
ops.reason: Baseline text is 'Free text query', which gives no example. The example word bolt comes from the source spec; the spec does not say which fields the text is matched against, so the text avoids claiming any.
Default 20 rows of 4 fields each is more than an agent usually needs to pick a candidate. 10 keeps answers short; the caller can still ask for up to 50.

ops.name: get_part
ops.reason: Shorter, and the verb get matches the upstream operation.

ops.text: Get one part by its part code, with its default fields. Says clearly when no part has that code. Read-only.
ops.reason: Drops the 'Source note' suffix from the upstream summary and states the not-found behaviour the server really has.

ops.text: The part code exactly as returned by find_parts, for example from the partId field.
ops.reason: Tells the agent where a valid code comes from, which avoids guessed codes.

It fetches up to 10 pages and filters them in memory, so it is slow and only reports scan coverage, not full results. find_parts with a text query covers most needs. Trade-off for the reviewer: this removes the feature-key filter from the server; revert this op if that filter matters.

ops.name: find_part_details
ops.description: Search parts by text, take the first match and return its details in one call. Says clearly when nothing matches. Read-only.

args.name: text
args.description: Words to look for in part names, for example bolt.

ops.reason: The most common two-step question (find a part, then read it) becomes one call, so an agent does not have to chain tools. It only uses the two existing read tools; the first match is the upstream ranking, not necessarily the best.
